newsitem.title: UGANDA: Heavy fighting rages on Ugandan-Zairean border.
newsitem.headline: Heavy fighting rages on Ugandan-Zairean border.

text.p: Heavy fighting raged on the border between Uganda and Zaire on Wednesday after some 100 Ugandan rebels from Zaire attacked Ugandan army positions on Tuesday night, Ugandan army officers said.
The fighting is around the villages of Buswangwe, Kisehere and Kyabitondo, near Uganda's southwestern provincial capital Kasese. Casualties have been heavy on both sides, they said.
Hundreds of residents have fled the area and the sound of heavy artillery fire was audible from the distance, said Kasese residents reached by telephone.
Displaced people are moving back to primary schools where they stayed during such an attack in November, they said.
"The fighting is still going on and it is heavy," one army officer told Reuters in Kampala.
On Tuesday the Ugandan army commander, Major-General Mugisha Muntu, said Ugandan troops had wiped out the rebels through a sortie three km (two miles) across the border.
The Ugandans say the rebels are from the mainly Moslem Allied Democratic Force (ADF), backed by Sudan and incorporating renegade Zairean soldiers.
In turn the Zairean government has accused Uganda of invading eastern Zaire in coordination with the Zairean rebels who now control vast tracts of the country.
The independent Kampala press continued on Wednesday to report Ugandan incursions deeper into Zairean territory.

The privately owned newspaper, the Monitor, quoted Lieutenant-Colonel Geoffrey Muheesi, commander of the Ugandan army's 307 Brigade, as saying the Ugandans had pursued rebels into the Zairean towns of Kasindi, Mutaga, Masabwa and Manda.

It said in an editorial it was concerned that the Ugandan army had not stopped Ugandan civilians from looting Zairean towns. "(They are) retreating with loads of mattresses, iron sheets and other goodies," it said.

"Apart from looting, there have been reports of rape and other aggravated acts of brutality inflicted by the soldiers on civilians in the war zone both in Uganda and Zaire," the Monitor said. It urged disciplinary action.
General Muntu told a parliamentary committee on Tuesday that the army pulled back inside Uganda after the sortie and had them reinforced on the border.
He denied that Ugandan troops helped ethnic Tutsi Banyamulenge rebels capture the Zairean town of Beni or took part in fighting for any other towns in northeastern Zaire.
